title: Tsallis Entropy: the q-Deformed Analogue of the Rényi Entropy Identity
description: The parent entry showed that Rényi entropy is the logarithm of a power mean, H_α(p) = −log(M_{α−1}(p,p)). This entry establishes the Tsallis-entropy analogue by replacing the ordinary logarithm with the q-deformed logarithm ln_q(x) = (x^{1−q}−1)/(1−q). It proves: the q-deformed (pseudo-additive) law of the logarithm ln_q(xy) = ln_q(x)+ln_q(y)+(1−q)·ln_q(x)·ln_q(y); the escort identity S_q(p) = −Σ pᵢ^q·ln_q(pᵢ) (exact q-analogue of Shannon's H = −Σ pᵢ log pᵢ); the bridge to Rényi S_q(p) = ln_q(exp(H_q(p))); the signature non-extensivity S_q(p⊗r) = S_q(p)+S_q(r)+(1−q)·S_q(p)·S_q(r) on product distributions; and the q→1 limit ln_q(x) → log(x) recovering the Shannon case. Fully machine-checked with 0 sorries and 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext:
Constantino Tsallis introduced his non-extensive entropy S_q in 1988 as a one-parameter generalization of the Boltzmann-Gibbs/Shannon entropy, motivated by systems with long-range interactions and multifractal structure. The central object is the q-deformed logarithm ln_q(x) = (x^{1−q}−1)/(1−q), which degenerates to the ordinary logarithm as q → 1, so that Tsallis entropy recovers Shannon entropy in the same limit.

The parent entry (amgm-inequality-oq-03-oq-04) unified Rényi entropy and power-mean monotonicity through the identity H_α(p) = −log(M_{α−1}(p,p)). Its open-questions list explicitly asked whether an analogous identity holds for Tsallis entropy, which uses the arithmetic q-deformed operations rather than the geometric/logarithmic ones. This entry answers that question affirmatively.
overview.problemStatement:
**Open Question** (amgm-inequality-oq-03-oq-04-oq-02): Establish the Tsallis-entropy analogue of the entropy identity underlying the AM-GM / Rényi lineage, replacing the geometric/log operations by the q-deformed arithmetic ones, and identify the equality/limit cases recovering the Shannon case as q → 1.

**Resolution**: With the q-logarithm ln_q(x) = (x^{1−q}−1)/(1−q) and Tsallis entropy S_q(p) = (1 − Σ pᵢ^q)/(q−1):

1. ln_q obeys the pseudo-additive law ln_q(xy) = ln_q(x)+ln_q(y)+(1−q)·ln_q(x)·ln_q(y).
2. S_q(p) = −Σ pᵢ^q·ln_q(pᵢ) (escort form) and S_q(p) = ln_q(exp(H_q(p))) (bridge to Rényi H_q).
3. Non-extensivity: S_q(p⊗r) = S_q(p)+S_q(r)+(1−q)·S_q(p)·S_q(r).
4. Limit: ln_q(x) → log(x) as q → 1, so the whole framework degenerates to the Shannon case.
overview.text: Tsallis entropy is the q-deformed analogue of Rényi entropy: replacing log by the q-logarithm ln_q turns the parent's identity H_α = −log(M_{α−1}) into S_q = ln_q(exp(H_q)), with a pseudo-additive (non-extensive) product law whose cross term (1−q)·S_q(p)·S_q(r) vanishes as q → 1, recovering Shannon entropy.
overview.proofStrategy:
The file is deliberately elementary and self-contained (it re-declares renyiEntropy locally rather than importing the parent):

1. **q-logarithm algebra** (qLog_mul): expand ln_q(xy) using (xy)^{1−q} = x^{1−q}·y^{1−q} (Real.mul_rpow) and clear denominators; the pseudo-additive law is a ring identity.

2. **Escort form** (tsallis_eq_neg_sum_qLog): the pointwise step pᵢ^q·ln_q(pᵢ) = (pᵢ − pᵢ^q)/(1−q) uses pᵢ^q·pᵢ^{1−q} = pᵢ (Real.rpow_add); summing and applying Σ pᵢ = 1 gives S_q.

3. **Bridge to Rényi** (tsallis_eq_qLog_exp_renyi): rewrite exp(H_q)^{1−q} = exp((1−q)·H_q) via Real.rpow_def_of_pos, simplify the exponent to log(Σ pᵢ^q), and use exp∘log = id (Σ pᵢ^q > 0).

4. **Non-extensivity** (tsallis_pseudo_additive): the escort sum of the product distribution factorizes, Σ_{(i,j)} (pᵢ rⱼ)^q = (Σ pᵢ^q)(Σ rⱼ^q), via Finset.sum_product and Finset.sum_mul_sum; the identity is then field algebra in (q−1).

5. **q→1 limit** (qLog_tendsto_log): ln_q(x) = (x^{1−q}−1)/(1−q) equals the slope at 0 of u ↦ exp(log x · u) after the substitution u = 1−q. That function has derivative log x at 0 (chain rule), so hasDerivAt_iff_tendsto_slope gives the limit on the punctured neighborhood 𝓝[≠] 1.
keyInsights: **q-deformation of the logarithm**: ln_q(x) = (x^{1−q}−1)/(1−q) is the unique deformation whose q→1 limit is log and whose product law carries a single cross term (1−q)·ln_q(x)·ln_q(y). That cross term is the whole story of non-extensivity.

**Escort weighting**: Tsallis entropy is −Σ pᵢ^q·ln_q(pᵢ), i.e. Shannon's −Σ pᵢ log pᵢ with log replaced by ln_q and the probabilities re-weighted by the escort powers pᵢ^q. Both replacements are needed for the identity to close.

**Same identity, deformed pair**: the parent's H_α = −log(M_{α−1}) becomes S_q = ln_q(exp(H_q)). Where Rényi uses the exp/log pair, Tsallis uses the q-exponential/q-logarithm pair; the two entropies are related by exactly this deformation.

**Non-extensivity is exact algebra**: S_q(p⊗r) = S_q(p)+S_q(r)+(1−q)·S_q(p)·S_q(r) is not an approximation — it is an exact identity, reducing to the factorization of the escort sum over a product distribution.
**The limit is a derivative**: recovering Shannon as q→1 is literally reading off the derivative of u ↦ x^u at u=0. The q-logarithm is the finite-difference slope; log is its limiting slope.
prerequisites: Real power, log, exp; derivative as a slope limit

conclusion.summary: We formalize the Tsallis-entropy analogue of the parent's Rényi/power-mean identity. Replacing the logarithm by the q-deformed logarithm ln_q gives: the pseudo-additive law of the q-logarithm, the escort form S_q = −Σ pᵢ^q·ln_q(pᵢ), the bridge S_q = ln_q(exp(H_q)), the non-extensive product law S_q(p⊗r) = S_q(p)+S_q(r)+(1−q)·S_q(p)·S_q(r), and the q→1 limit ln_q(x) → log(x). All results are fully machine-checked with 0 sorries and 0 axioms.
conclusion.implications:
**Unification across a one-parameter family**: the parent entry sits at the q→1 limit of this family. The bridge S_q = ln_q(exp(H_q)) shows Rényi and Tsallis entropy are the same information content viewed through two members (exp/log vs q-exp/q-log) of the same deformation.

**Non-extensivity made exact**: the product law is an exact algebraic identity, which is what makes Tsallis entropy the natural entropy for composing independent subsystems with a tunable interaction parameter q.
openQuestions: Does the pseudo-additive law extend to a concavity/monotonicity statement for S_q in q, paralleling the parent's Rényi monotonicity?
Can the q→1 recovery be lifted from ln_q to the full entropy, proving S_q(p) → −Σ pᵢ log pᵢ as q → 1 by continuity of the finite sum?
Is there a q-deformed power-mean M^{(q)}_r whose q-logarithm reproduces S_q directly, completing the analogy with the parent's H_α = −log(M_{α−1})?
